Compare two or three plants side by side. Open a plant in the plant picker and choose Compare; once two are chosen, “Compare 2” at the foot of the picker opens a table with a column for each. What you’ve chosen stays while you search and filter, and clears when you close the picker or choose Clear.

The table puts first the facts where they differ: height and width, sun, water, hardiness and whether each is hardy where your garden is, bloom and flower color, form and winter leaves, native status, poison to the people and pets in your yard, caterpillars and pollinators, deer, growth rate, and the plan’s own warnings for any already placed. The facts that are the same for all are folded below.

Under each value it says where it’s from and how sure it is, in the same words as a plant’s details: NC State, USDA or a nursery page; confirmed by a second source, one source only, or given for its species; read from a description and kept only because a second reading agreed. A fact no source gives says Not known. Nothing is ranked or recommended.

Each column has its own Place button (Swap, when you came to swap a plant) and Remove. On a phone two plants show at once, with the third a sideways scroll away and the facts’ names kept in view; on a computer, all three.
